rationale: The foundational cohort defining Ramond-Elliott neurodevelopmental syndrome (RAMELN, OMIM #621421) described by Ramond et al. (2023; PMID 36549593) comprises exactly 12 affected individuals across 11 unrelated families. All 12 individuals presented with developmental delay or intellectual disability (12/12, 100%), alongside hallmark features of hypotonia (10/12, 83.3%), microcephaly/subnormal head circumference (10/12, 83.3%), and infantile spasms in a subset (6/12, 50%). There is no peer-reviewed cohort establishing a primary denominator of 15; rather, subsequent reports evaluate single additional cases, solidifying N=12 as the landmark cohort denominator.

evidence.text: Ramond et al. (2023) recruited 12 individuals from 11 unrelated families carrying monoallelic variants clustered in the 5' region of TRA2B, all of whom presented with intellectual disability and/or developmental delay (12/12), frequently associated with microcephaly, hypotonia, and infantile spasms.

source.title: Clustered variants in the 5' coding region of TRA2B cause a distinctive neurodevelopmental syndrome
source.quote: A total of 12 individuals from 11 unrelated families who harbored predicted loss-of-function monoallelic variants, mostly de novo, were recruited... All affected individuals presented intellectual disability and/or developmental delay, frequently associated with infantile spasms, microcephaly, brain anomalies, autism spectrum disorder, feeding difficulties, and short stature.

evidence.text: Australian Genomics PanelApp curation for TRA2B and Ramond-Elliott neurodevelopmental syndrome (MIM# 621421) records phenotypic frequencies evaluated across the standard denominator of 12, citing 6/12 for infantile spasms alongside hypotonia.

new_directions.question_text: What are the exact prevalence rates of non-neurological features (such as cardiac anomalies, feeding difficulties, or skeletal findings) in expanded multi-center TRA2B patient registries beyond the initial 12 individuals?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying non-neurological manifestations will help distinguish Ramond-Elliott syndrome clinically from other spliceosomopathies and early infantile epileptic encephalopathies with overlapping hypotonia and microcephaly.

new_directions.question_text: Does variant position within the 5' region of TRA2B correlate with the severity of microcephaly (-4 SD vs milder subnormal head circumference) or drug responsiveness of infantile spasms?
new_directions.rationale: Initial studies show clustering of variants upstream of an alternative translation initiation site; testing whether specific positions alter the relative expression of Tra2β-3 could explain the phenotypic variability observed in the cohort.
